headword: {平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}

definitions.explanation: International activities — usually organized by the United Nations — in which troops, police, and civilian personnel are dispatched to former conflict zones to monitor ceasefires, protect civilians, and support the restoration of stability. In Japanese political discussion, the term is strongly associated with the UN PKO framework and Japan's own Self-Defense Forces participation.

⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧わたって{平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}して→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧きた。

examples.japanese: ⟦{自衛隊|じえいたい}→自衛隊：05790_jieitai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{国連|こくれん}→国連：12035_kokuren⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一環|いっかん}→一環：17696_ikkan⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{南|みなみ}→南：00652_minami⟧スーダン⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{派遣|はけん}→派遣：13273_haken⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: The Self-Defense Forces have been dispatched to South Sudan as part of the United Nations' peacekeeping operations.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧ (peace), ⟦{維持|いじ}→維持：01624_iji⟧ (maintenance, upholding), and ⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧ (activity, operations). A direct calque of the English phrase "peacekeeping operations." It is the standard Japanese term for UN-led missions that send personnel to former conflict zones to monitor ceasefires and help stabilize the situation, and is often abbreviated in news reports as PKO.

USAGE:
- Written out in full in formal contexts (government documents, news reporting on missions); abbreviated as PKO in headlines and speech.
- Usually associated with the UN: {国連|こくれん}{平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう} (United Nations peacekeeping operations).
- In Japan this term is tightly linked to the 1992 PKO law ({国際平和協力法|こくさいへいわきょうりょくほう}), which first allowed the Self-Defense Forces to be dispatched overseas.

POLITICAL NOTE:
Japan's constitutional pacifism makes any overseas deployment of the Self-Defense Forces politically sensitive. {平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう} has therefore been one of the main channels through which Japan contributes militarily abroad — under strict conditions, including the "Five Principles for Participation" (e.g., a ceasefire must already be in place, and consent of the host country is required).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {国連|こくれん}{平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}: United Nations peacekeeping operations
- {平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}する→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧: to participate in peacekeeping operations
- {平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}⟦{部隊|ぶたい}→部隊：28119_butai⟧: a peacekeeping unit
- {平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一環|いっかん}→一環：17696_ikkan⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧: as part of peacekeeping operations
- {平和維持活動|へいわいじかつどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{展開|てんかい}する→展開する：25229_tenkaisuru⟧: to deploy peacekeeping operations

SIMILAR WORDS:
- PKO (ピーケーオー): the common abbreviation used in news and speech
- {平和維持軍|へいわいじぐん}: peacekeeping force — the armed unit carrying out the operations
- ⟦{国際協力|こくさいきょうりょく}→国際協力：22688_kokusaikyouryoku⟧: international cooperation — a broader umbrella term
- ⟦{人道支援|じんどうしえん}→人道支援：18890_jindoushien⟧: humanitarian aid — distinct from peacekeeping, focused on relief rather than ceasefire monitoring
